findings.headline: 99215 share is 7.1x expected and high for every complexity level; charts support a lower level on 70% of sampled 99215s
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 30.8% against 4.3% expected (z_adj 21.2). It is 20.8% on patients with no chronic conditions, where peers are at 2.1%. In a random sample of 30 charts, 9 support a lower level than billed, including 7 of the 10 99215s (peer rate 15%). Note checks did not show inflated notes. Draft overpayment estimate from the random sample: $24,843 (CI $15,722–$33,964). Needs human review.

findings.headline: 45.6% of visits billed as 99215; charts support a lower level on 69% of sampled 99215s
findings.interpretation: The panel is somewhat sicker than average, but the 99215 share is above peers at every complexity level (34% at one condition vs 3.5%). Random sample of 30 charts, completed after a follow-up: 11 below billed level, including 9 of the 13 99215s. Draft estimate $3,464 (CI $2,415–$4,513).

findings.headline: Healthy panel billed at 6.6x expected 99215; charts support a lower level on 78% of documented 99215s
findings.interpretation: About half of this panel's visits are for low-complexity patients, yet 10% of zero-condition visits are 99215 vs 2.1% for peers. Chart review: 7 of the 9 documented 99215s are below the billed level (peer rate 25%). Draft estimate $1,732 (CI $1,200–$2,264).

findings.headline: Healthy panel billed 99215 at 9.9x expected; notes appear inflated to match the bill (audit trail shows bulk-created and paste-heavy notes)
findings.interpretation: 65% of visits are for low-complexity patients, and 16.8% of zero-condition visits are 99215 vs 2.1% for peers. On their face the charts mostly support the level billed (only 10% below). But 47% of notes address more problems than the claim diagnoses support. 20% describe data review that the claim's lab lines and orders do not show. 27% are duplicates. The audit trail shows 17% bulk-created and 20% paste-heavy notes. The automated review could not decide, so this leaning is my own judgment from note-versus-claim evidence. That evidence is weaker than charts that show a lower level, so it needs careful human review. There is no overpayment estimate, because the charts as written support the billed level.

findings.headline: Healthy panel billed 99215 at 11x expected, but only 12 of 30 random charts were returned
findings.interpretation: 81% of visits are low-complexity, and 27% of one-condition visits are 99215. In the 12 charts returned, 2 support a lower level (17%, close to the peer rate), and note checks suggest inflation: 67% problem mismatch, 25% data without tests. The follow-up for missing visits got no response, and the office refused the audit trail. Too few charts to conclude. Non-response is not evidence.
